target_customer: AI labs, governments, defense organizations and owners of stalled infrastructure sites with unused power
problem: Data centers wait years for grid power while delayed construction sites sit on unused interconnects. Pacific builds factory made modular GPU pods that deploy on those sites in days.
business_model: Hardware pod sales, managed GPU rental and colocation

founders.name: Harper Dammann Smith
education: Dropped out of an aerospace engineering program (school not named)
previous_startups: Drone startup grown to $1M revenue at 18
Sold a first company (name not given)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he shot expeditions for Red Bull on 7,000m peaks.

competitors.name: Crusoe Spark
competitors.what: Modular AI data center units of about 1 MW

competitors.name: Armada
competitors.what: Prefabricated modular AI data centers (Galleon, Orion)
competitors.funding_then: reported $230M Series B at $2B valuation (aggregator headline)

technical_complexity.rationale: Containerized B300 GPU pods with cooling, power and deployment on third party sites need hardware manufacturing, thermal design and supply chain execution beyond a six person team.

defensibility.rationale: Better funded rivals already ship modular units; the claimed diamond wafer cooling and vertical integration of transformers are plans, not shown.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Well funded modular players were already shipping in 2026. No move against Pacific found.

market_need_then: Reports in 2026 count at least 47 large US data center projects delayed, withdrawn or blocked, and grid power is the main constraint, which supports the stalled site pitch. Letters of intent cited by the company are non-binding.

identity.voice_and_tone: Ambitious, space and compute at scale

branding.brand_signature: Pods named by GPU count (Pod 32) and compute across the galaxy ambition

brand_strength.rationale: Little outside coverage found; a brand search surfaced unrelated companies.

outcome_analysis: Pacific is a Summer 2026 hardware company with six people, no disclosed funding and no exit or layoff reports. Its pitch matches a real power bottleneck, but it faces funded modular rivals and needs a factory and capital. Outcome is open, so no factors are assigned.
notes: No funding found. YC page cites $95M in non-binding letters of intent for hosted compute and $27M for pod sales, and says the first factory is potentially funded by Missouri; unconfirmed. Company site names no founder; the YC page names Harper Dammann Smith; site contact says Harper Smith. Founder education school is not named.
